title: 2.1.6 Write Your First if
description: Write an if statement that logs a message when a number meets a threshold. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: designed: practice for 'The if Statement', book 2.1.1

steps.title: Declare a number variable
steps.instructions: Create a variable called score and assign it a number value of your choice.

steps.title: Write an if statement
steps.instructions: Write an if statement that checks whether score is greater than or equal to 70. Inside the if block, use console.log to print a message saying the score passes.

requirements.title: if statement checks score >= 70
requirements.description: if statement's condition compares score to 70 with >=. Help: 2.1.3 (If / Else if / Else)

requirements.title: console.log runs inside the if block
requirements.description: console.log is called inside the score >= 70 if block. Help: 2.1.3 (If / Else if / Else)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.1.6 Write Your First if". The task they were given: Create a variable called score and assign it a number value of your choice. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
